meta: Facial prices in Bali in 2026: what you pay for a Hydrafacial, a Korean facial, a face massage or a body treatment in Uluwatu, with tax included.
intro: Facial prices in Bali vary a lot: a 30-minute facial in a small salon and an 80-minute Korean Hydrafacial are not the same treatment. This guide explains what drives the price, what to watch out for, and exactly what you pay at Point Face in Uluwatu.
body_html:
What changes the price of a facial in Bali

  • Duration: 30, 60 or 80 minutes makes a big difference.
  • Technology: hydrodermabrasion, LED, radiofrequency and ultrasonic devices cost more than a manual facial.
  • Products: authentic Korean or professional brands vs unbranded creams.
  • Expertise: facial specialists vs all-round therapists.
  • Hidden fees: many venues add tax and service charge on top of the menu price. Always ask.

Is a Hydrafacial in Bali worth it?

A Korean Hydrafacial combines several steps that would be separate treatments elsewhere: exfoliation, extraction, hydrodermabrasion, serum infusion and LED. You leave with visible glow and no downtime, which is why most of our guests choose it over a basic facial.

How to get the best value

  1. Choose one facial matched to your main concern rather than several small treatments.
  2. Add a face massage (Buccal from IDR 250K) instead of booking a second session.
  3. Book early in your trip, then a second facial before you fly home.
  4. Ask about our current offers on Instagram @pointfacebali.
